mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used 1VD-FTV engine costs £2,000-£4,500 supply-only; reconditioned units are £4,500-£7,500; fully rebuilt engines range from £6,000-£10,000 supply-only [EM-QUOTE]. Fitting adds approximately £1,500-£2,500 in labour at an independent 4x4 specialist.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of injector failure in a Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common symptoms are long crank times when starting (hot-cranking), grey smoke on tip-in acceleration, rail-pressure hunting at idle, loss of power and poor fuel economy. Worn injectors are often the beginning of a failure cascade that can damage the engine.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8 (2008-2018) is worth approximately £15,000-£45,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. A reconditioned or rebuilt engine at £4,500-£10,000 supply-only represents 15-40% of the vehicle's value - which is generally viable, especially given the Land Cruiser's legendary durability and strong residual values.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the single-turbo and twin-turbo 1VD-FTV?

acceptedAnswer.text: The single-turbo variant produces 202hp and 430Nm of torque, fitted to the 70-Series Land Cruiser (VDJ76/78/79). The twin-turbo variant produces 282hp and 650Nm of torque, fitted to the 200-Series Land Cruiser (VDJ200). The twin-turbo offers significantly more power and torque for towing and motorway driving.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 V8 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional engine replacement on a Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8 typically takes 15-20 working hours for an experienced 4x4 specialist. Allow 4-7 working days from workshop drop-off to collection, depending on parts availability and workshop workload.

mainEntity.name: How reliable is the Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8 1VD-FTV engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1VD-FTV is one of the most reliable diesel V8s ever built, with a nigh-indestructible graphite cast iron cylinder block. Many examples exceed 300,000 miles with proper maintenance. However, it has known weak points: injector wear (past 250,000-300,000 km), turbocharger VNT vane seizure, early oil consumption (pre-2010, resolved with vacuum pump replacement), DPF issues on Euro-spec models (2015 onwards) and water pump seal failure.

historyTimeline.h2: Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8 - powered by the 1VD-FTV engine - is Toyota's first and only production V8 diesel. Launched in 2007, this 4.5-litre twin-turbocharged diesel engine delivered the combination of immense torque, legendary off-road capability and the durability that defines the Land Cruiser name. Available in both single-turbo (70-Series) and twin-turbo (200-Series) configurations, the 1VD-FTV remains one of the most respected diesel V8s ever built.

milestones.description: **2007** - 1VD-FTV engine introduced globally; single-turbo variant debuts in 70-Series Land Cruiser (Australia); twin-turbo variant debuts in 200-Series Land Cruiser wagon
**2008** - Land Cruiser V8 launched in the UK on 15 February, priced at £55,995
**2008-2011** - Early UK models produce 282bhp and 650Nm of torque through a six-speed automatic transmission
**2010** - Early oil consumption issues resolved with vacuum pump and oil separator revisions
**2015** - DPF systems introduced on European-spec models from 2015 model year

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h3: The Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8 (1VD-FTV) is one of the most respected diesel V8s ever built, with a nigh-indestructible graphite cast iron cylinder block. However, even the toughest engines have weaknesses. Injector wear, turbocharger issues, oil consumption and DPF problems can lead to expensive repairs. Rebuilt 1VD-FTV engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Injector Failure - Why the Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 V8 Loses Power and Economy
problems.affectedModels: Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8 (1VD-FTV, high mileage)
problems.rootCause: As Denso common-rail injectors wear, they can cause long crank times, grey smoke on tip-in, rail-pressure hunting at idle and eventual loss of power. Worn injectors are often the beginning of a failure cascade that can damage the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all 8 Denso injectors; Denso 095000-9790 or Toyota 23670-51070/59055
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; engine otherwise healthy
Best if other issues present or high mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8 (2008-2018) is worth approximately £15,000-£45,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. Given the high value of these vehicles, engine replacement is almost always financially viable - a rebuilt engine at £7,000-£11,000 fitted represents 15-40% of the vehicle's value. For vehicles worth over £20,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is the smartest investment.
problems.recommendation: If your Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 V8 is experiencing long crank times, grey smoke on acceleration or rough idle, have the injectors tested immediately. Injector replacement at a specialist is significantly cheaper than dealer prices. If the engine has high mileage or other issues like turbo wear or oil consumption, a full replacement with a reconditioned 1VD-FTV unit is the most reliable long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 1VD-FTV Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 V8 engine prices

problems.h4: Turbocharger Failure - Why the Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 V8 Loses Boost
problems.affectedModels: Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8 (1VD-FTV, twin-turbo, high mileage)
problems.rootCause: The 200-Series Land Cruiser has a twin-turbo setup with left and right bank turbos. Common failures include VNT vane seizure due to soot buildup, electronic actuator faults leading to limp mode and loss of top-end power, and dust ingress damaging the turbochargers.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable if only one turbo failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace both turbochargers; inspect oil supply lines

problems.recommendation: Turbo failure on the Land Cruiser 4.5 V8 is often preceded by injector wear. If you're replacing turbos, have the injectors tested and the oil supply lines inspected. For high-mileage Land Cruiser 4.5 V8 examples, a full replacement with a reconditioned 1VD-FTV engine often makes more sense than investing in piecemeal turbo repairs.
problems.cta: -> Compare Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 V8 engine replacement prices

problems.h4: Oil Consumption & DPF Issues - Long-Term Reliability Concerns
problems.affectedModels: Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 D-4D V8 (1VD-FTV, pre-2010 and Euro-spec)
problems.rootCause: Early (pre-2010) 1VD-FTV engines suffered from excessive oil consumption, sometimes up to 1 litre per 1,000 km. This was often resolved by replacing the vacuum pump or oil separator. On Euro-spec models from 2015 onwards, DPF systems can clog, especially with urban driving.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace vacuum pump or oil separator
repairOptions.longevity: Viable for early oil consumption issues
Viable if DPF is only partially blocked

problems.recommendation: If your Toyota Land Cruiser 4.5 V8 is consuming oil and is a pre-2010 model, have the vacuum pump and oil separator checked first - this often resolves the issue at minimal cost. For DPF issues, regular motorway driving helps prevent clogging. If the engine has multiple issues or very high mileage, a full replacement with a reconditioned 1VD-FTV engine offers the best long-term reliability.
